title: Official-source candidates from the July industry digest

selectedGap.reason: No published or pending public demand source currently represents the procurement authority issuer lane.

guardrailNotes: The private email digest was used only to discover leads; every candidate claim below is supported by a durable public source.
All records remain private candidate_pending objects until Andrew reviews, edits, accepts, and explicitly publishes them in Admin Review.
Agreement-in-principle and consortium language is preserved and must not be presented as a completed procurement, endorsement, or guaranteed workshare.
Foreign, generic, weakly sourced, or low-fit newsletter items were not converted into candidates.

candidates.reviewerRationale: This is the first candidate in the missing procurement-authority demand lane and records a major public Canadian naval acquisition without converting preferred-supplier negotiations into a final contract. Official Defence Investment Agency evidence supports the intended fleet size, operational needs, schedule, sustainment direction, and Canadian industrial participation. Reviewers should preserve the public-source caveat and update the record when negotiations produce binding requirements.

sources.title: Government of Canada advances Canadian Patrol Submarine Project
sources.locator: Preferred-supplier negotiations, fleet intent, schedule, operational needs, and industrial participation
sources.summary: The official backgrounder documents preferred-supplier negotiations for up to twelve conventionally powered submarines with long-range, long-endurance, under-ice, surveillance, deterrence, sustainment, and Canadian industrial participation objectives.

fieldEvidence.excerpt: The official backgrounder supports a procurement-stage Canadian submarine program with preferred-supplier negotiations, a planned fleet of up to twelve boats, and first delivery targeted for 2034.
Canada identifies long range, long endurance, under-ice operation, surveillance, deterrence, Arctic, Atlantic, and Pacific missions as public capability needs for the future fleet.
The public notice calls for Canadian industrial participation and a domestic sustainment approach covering infrastructure, training, maintenance, and through-life support.

demandSource.title: Canadian Patrol Submarine Project preferred-supplier negotiations
demandSource.summary: Canada has selected TKMS as preferred supplier for negotiations on up to twelve conventionally powered submarines, while defining public operational, schedule, sustainment, and Canadian industrial-participation objectives.

requirements.title: Future submarine operational capability
requirements.problemStatement: Canada requires a future submarine fleet able to operate at long range and endurance, including under ice, while supporting surveillance, deterrence, and sovereignty missions across Arctic, Atlantic, and Pacific approaches.
requirements.desiredEndState: Deliver an initial submarine in 2034 and build toward a fleet of up to twelve interoperable conventionally powered submarines without creating a capability gap as the Victoria class retires.
requirements.publicCaveat: Public-source alignment only. This is not procurement eligibility, endorsement, customer interest, or a classified requirement.

requirements.title: Canadian submarine sustainment and industrial capacity
requirements.problemStatement: Canada needs domestic infrastructure, workforce, training, maintenance, supply-chain, and through-life support capacity so the future submarine fleet can remain available and sovereignly sustained over decades.
requirements.desiredEndState: Establish a durable Canadian industrial and sustainment base that can support fleet introduction, maintenance, upgrades, training, and operational availability throughout the new submarine program.
requirements.publicCaveat: Public-source alignment only. This is not procurement eligibility, endorsement, customer interest, or a classified requirement.

candidates.reviewerRationale: Telesat is a material missing Canadian space and secure-connectivity company. Official sources support its Ottawa identity, global satellite operations, government and maritime customer focus, Lightspeed LEO network, and an agreement in principle for secure Arctic Mil-Ka services. Reviewers must retain agreement-in-principle language and avoid implying that the definitive ESCP-P contract is already executed.
